A1.justification: Both PDFs describe the same work by the same authors. All 20 pages of v3 and 22 pages of v4, including appendices, support comparison. Theorems, proofs and simulation tables can be matched across relocation and renumbering.

before.justification: Section 5.3 and Table 1 report original simulations comparing matrix confidence-bound lengths. Appendix B and Table 2 report corresponding scalar simulations.

after.justification: Section 5.3 and Appendices B.2–B.3 report original matrix and scalar simulations, including the expanded matrix comparison in Table 3.

M1.justification: V4 introduces a confidence-bound procedure using variance estimated from disjoint observation pairs as its main independent-sample result. V3’s classical sample-variance procedure is retained with a tightened correction in Appendix B.3. The self-normalized procedure remains unchanged.

E1.justification: Both versions evaluate matrix mean estimation using synthetic matrices with independent uniform eigenvalues, alongside scalar Uniform[0,1] simulations. The additional variance-bound comparison introduces no new dataset, population or test scenario.

E2.justification: The matrix comparison expands from classical-variance and self-normalized bounds to paired-variance, classical-variance and self-normalized bounds in v4 Table 3. The oracle Bennett-Bernstein reference and the scalar comparators in Table 2 are retained.

E3.justification: The stated simulations retain dimension 3, the same matrix-generation procedure, alpha = 0.05, five sample sizes from 100 to 1,000,000, and bound-length ratios relative to the oracle. V4 Table 3 extends this protocol without documenting changed evaluation settings.

E4.justification: Appendix B.3 and Table 3 add a targeted comparison of paired versus classical variance estimation within the union-bound approach. This examines how variance-estimator choice affects confidence-set tightness, a comparison absent from v3.

E5.justification: Both versions report simulation ratios without replicate counts, seeds, standard errors, error bars or significance tests. The nominal 95% confidence level describes the bounds being evaluated and remains unchanged.

E6.justification: At n = 1,000, the classical-bound ratio changes from 2.315 in v3 Table 1 to 1.874 in v4 Table 3; the new paired bound gives 1.589. Self-normalized ratios also change, including 1.354 to 1.397 at n = 100 and 1.120 to 1.105 at n = 1,000, without a documented procedure change. Scalar Table 2 is unchanged.

T1.justification: V4 Theorem 3.1 supplies a new paired-variance proof using two Bennett-Bernstein applications, obtaining a variance-independent lower-order correction of order 1/n up to logarithms. Strengthened square-root comparisons in Lemma A.1 also tighten the retained classical bound. V3 Corollary 4.3’s auxiliary bound, Equation (40), and its derivation are removed; the primary self-normalized guarantee and sharpness proof remain.

C1.justification: Proposition 1.1 redefines the first headline contribution around paired variance and an O(log(nd/alpha)/n) remainder, replacing the previous variance-dependent remainder. This strengthens a principal finite-sample claim while retaining the overarching first-order sharpness and martingale-validity claims.

C2.justification: Sections 3 and B.3 explain why classical variance estimation can nevertheless yield a looser confidence bound and discuss improving its analysis. Section 6 adds computational-simplicity versus tightness and anytime-validity tradeoffs. Appendix C clarifies that nonclosed-form scalar betting intervals can outperform the paper’s sharpness criterion.

D1.justification: Section 3 explicitly instructs discarding one observation when the sample size is odd for the paired procedure. Section 6 adds that both approaches require O(n) steps, with smaller computational constants for the first. These are added operational and computational details.

R1.justification: V4 adds Orabona and Jun (2024) and expands Appendix C’s existing discussion of Shekhar and Ramdas to explain the relationship to minimax-optimal, nonclosed-form betting intervals. The earlier PAC-Bayes review is retained; most other reference edits update bibliographic metadata.

P1.justification: Targeted introduction and summary rewrites accompany appendix reorganization. The classical theorem moves to Appendix B.3, Lemma 4.1’s proof moves to A.4, and auxiliary Bernstein material moves from A.2 to B.1. The overall six-section main-text sequence remains.

P2.justification: V4 adds Table 3, repeating Table 1’s paired and self-normalized columns alongside a classical-bound column. Table 1 is placed after its simulation discussion, and appendix material is reflowed. The table formatting and single-column page design remain consistent.

improvement.justification: V4 improves the independent-sample contribution by removing the variance-sensitive lower-order penalty highlighted in v3, while retaining and tightening the classical alternative. The direct variant comparison and clearer limitations improve interpretation. The overall gain is limited because first-order sharpness and the self-normalized method remain unchanged; the paired procedure’s even-sample restriction has an explicit workaround.
